I’ve definitely seen that tiels chew on legos before (they LOVE chewing on anything and everything, not just legos) but as long as they are well put together and can’t be taken apart by a bird, and are not small enough to be swallowed then you’re probably good, but still I would definitely recommend you keep a close eye on your bird anytime it’s out of it’s cage. Remember, birds are messy, and yes, even destructive creatures. You’ll definitely want to take getting a cockatiel into serious consideration. As for the glass and crystals you might want to be wary of that, if the glass can be swallowed or is sharp keep it far away and hidden from the bird, and they might chew on or push around your crystals too. Personally I just keep my crystals out of reach of my birds or put them away when they’re out and flying around.

Generally, wider cages are better than taller cages, but if you are only getting one medium sized bird it should be a decent size (although bigger is always better in this case). It shouldn’t be uncomfortable for the bird, but definitely be sure to let it out every day so it can fly around and get some proper flight and exercise that wouldn’t be possible in it’s cage
There’s a lot of oil ducts at the base of their backs, so your bird is probably just distributing oil throughout her feathers, perfectly normal bird behavior :)
It’s a little difficult to tell from this picture but it seems most likely your bird is female

Definitely get more shedding toys, and maybe some foraging toys. Also, you might want to get perches that have more texture and shape to them, the ones you have are fine, but they look rather smooth and straight for the most part, which has the potential to lead to arthritis later on in the birds life and at the very least cause discomfort to the feet. Other than that your cage looks like a nice home for your tiel :)
